blocks.text: Great work on the vowels! Now let's add your first consonant sound: K. The five kana in this row are just K plus each vowel you already know: ka, ki, ku, ke, ko. Say them out loud as you go — it really helps them stick.

blocks.hint: Looks like a person kicking a ball — KA-pow!
Like a KEY with two teeth on the left.
Like a KEG lying on its side with a tap.
Two short lines — a COrd coiled up.

blocks.text: Chant the whole row in a rhythm: KA KI KU KE KO. Every consonant row follows this same a-i-u-e-o order, so this pattern will serve you again and again.
か き く け こ あ か き え こ
blocks.title: Read this aloud

templates.hint: K plus a.
Think KEY.
The bird's beak.
Think KEG.
Two short lines.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ka"?
questions.explanation: か is ka — the one that looks like a person kicking.

questions.prompt: How do you read か?
questions.explanation: か is K plus a = ka.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ki"?
questions.explanation: き is ki — think of a KEY.

questions.prompt: How do you read き?
questions.explanation: き is K plus i = ki.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ku"?
questions.explanation: く is ku — the bird's beak shape.

questions.prompt: How do you read く?
questions.explanation: く is K plus u = ku.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ke"?
questions.explanation: け is ke — think of a KEG.

questions.prompt: How do you read け?
questions.explanation: け is K plus e = ke.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ko"?
questions.explanation: こ is ko — two short coiled lines.

questions.prompt: How do you read the word こ え?
questions.explanation: こ is ko and え is e, so こ え is ko e — it means voice.

notes: Spaces go between words, never between the kana of one word: write こえ (koe), not こ え (ko e), in examples, readings, prompts and choices. Choose example words an adult traveller would use, such as えき (station), over rare ones such as かき (persimmon).

original_draft.title: Reading real words with every sound

blocks.text: ともだち と がっこう。 おかあさん の しゃしん。 ちょっと みて。
blocks.title: Read this

blocks.text: Nice work! These are real words with every tricky sound you have learned: long vowels like おかあさん and がっこう, the small っ in ちょっと and がっこう, and the small ゃ in しゃしん. Read each word slowly and let your eyes catch every kana.
Watch the small っ. In がっこう you pause slightly before こ. In ちょっと you pause before と. That tiny gap is real — say it!
Watch the long vowels. おかあさん has a long お-あ sound, and がっこう ends in a long こ-う sound. Stretch them out.
The small ゃ joins with し in しゃしん, so し + ゃ = しゃ, one quick sound. Don't say two separate sounds.

templates.hint: Read ともだち out loud, then type what you hear.
Remember the small っ pause and the long こう sound.
Stretch the long お-あ at the start.
し + ゃ is one quick sound: しゃ.
Small ょ joins ち, then a small っ pause before と.

questions.prompt: In the passage, which word means "friend"?
questions.explanation: ともだち means friend. It is the very first word in the passage.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: ともだち
questions.explanation: ともだち — four plain kana, no tricky sounds here.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means "school"?
questions.explanation: がっこう means school. Note the small っ pause and the long こう sound.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: がっこう
questions.explanation: がっこう — small っ for the pause, and こう is a long vowel.

questions.prompt: Whose photograph is in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage says おかあさん の しゃしん — mother's photograph.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: おかあさん
questions.explanation: おかあさん — the お-あ at the start is a long vowel, so write both kana.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means "photograph"?
questions.explanation: しゃしん means photograph. The し + ゃ makes one quick しゃ sound.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: しゃしん
questions.explanation: しゃしん — remember the small ゃ joins し to make しゃ.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means "a little"?
questions.explanation: ちょっと means a little. It has a small ょ and a small っ pause.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: ちょっと
questions.explanation: ちょっと — ち + small ょ, then a small っ pause before と.

notes: When GRAMMAR TAUGHT SO FAR is (none), the passage may use only words the learner knows: no particles such as と, の, を, に, が or か, and no verb forms such as みて. Write it as labels or a short list (for example captions on photos), and make every comprehension question answerable from known words alone. Describe a long vowel by the kana that is held: in おかあさん the あ makes か last two beats (it is not お-あ), and in がっこう the う makes こ last two beats. Word typed checks as "Read this word and type how it sounds: <word>", never "type it in kana", because learners type rōmaji.

blocks.text: Time to make your first real sentences! In Japanese, you can say 'A is B' with a simple pattern: A は B です. Think of it as 'A, as for it, is B.'
The word です (desu) goes at the end. It's like 'is' or 'am' or 'are.' It makes your sentence polite and finished. Super useful — you'll use it constantly.

blocks.japanese: わたし は いしゃ です 。

blocks.text: See that は? Here's the tricky part: when は is used this way (as a topic marker), you read it as 'wa', NOT 'ha'. The spelling stays は, but the sound is 'wa'. It marks the topic — the thing you're talking about.
は points at your topic like a little sign saying 'as for THIS...'. And remember: topic は is pronounced 'wa'.

blocks.japanese: あなた は せんせい です 。
ともだち は がくせい です 。

blocks.text: To ask a question, just add か at the end: あなた は いしゃ です か 。 means 'Are you a doctor?' Easy, right?

blocks.label: Listen to A は B です sentences

templates.hint: Find the topic marker — remember it's read 'wa' here
Put は right after the topic (the thing you're talking about)
です means 'is/am/are' and sits at the end
Finish the sentence with です

questions.prompt: Which word means 'is / am / are' and ends a sentence?
questions.explanation: です goes at the end and means 'is/am/are'. It makes the sentence polite.

questions.prompt: Finish the sentence: わたし は がくせい ___ 。 (I am a student.)
questions.explanation: A は B です — the sentence ends with です.

questions.prompt: In あなた は せんせい です 。 how is は pronounced?
questions.explanation: When は is a topic marker, you read it 'wa', even though it's spelled は.

questions.prompt: Type this sentence in kana: 'My friend is a doctor.' (friend = ともだち, doctor = いしゃ)
questions.correctAnswer: ともだち は いしゃ です
questions.explanation: Topic ともだち, then は, then いしゃ, then です. Great work!

notes: Teach only this lesson's grammar. Do not preview the next grammar point (the A は B です draft taught か, which is the next lesson's target). Wrong choices must also be taught words or grammar, so no untaught particles such as か or を as distractors. Include at least one check that asks what a whole sentence means. In a typed sentence check, say "rōmaji is fine" so the learner knows no Japanese keyboard is needed. Put 。 straight after the last word, with no space before it.

blocks.text: Have you noticed the tiny っ inside some words? It is a small version of つ, and it is special. It has no sound of its own. Instead, it is a short silent beat — a little pause — right before the next sound.
Here is the one rule: when you see a small っ, stop for one beat, then hit the next sound a bit harder. Think of it like holding your breath for a split second before the next letter pops out.
Let's read your new words out loud. Pause where the っ sits, then say the next sound strongly: がっこう (school) — say 'ga', pause, then 'kkou'.
Small っ = a speed bump. You slow down, pause, then go again. If you forget the pause, がっこう turns into 'gakou' and sounds wrong!

blocks.label: Listen to the small っ pause

templates.hint: You go here to learn. Pause at っ: ga-(pause)-kkou.
Doing something with someone. i-(pause)-ssho.
Means 'a little'. cho-(pause)-tto.
You need this to ride a train. ki-(pause)-ppu.
Something you read with pictures and articles. za-(pause)-sshi.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'school'?
questions.explanation: がっこう is 'school'. Pause at the っ: ga-(pause)-kkou.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: がっこう
questions.explanation: Nice! がっこう — remember the little pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means '(doing) together'?
questions.explanation: いっしょ means 'together'. Say i-(pause)-ssho.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: いっしょ
questions.explanation: Great! いっしょ with a short pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'a little'?
questions.explanation: ちょっと means 'a little'. Pause: cho-(pause)-tto.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: ちょっと
questions.explanation: Perfect! ちょっと — don't forget the pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'ticket'?
questions.explanation: きっぷ means 'ticket'. Say ki-(pause)-ppu.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: きっぷ
questions.explanation: Yes! きっぷ with the little pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'magazine'?
questions.explanation: ざっし means 'magazine'. Pause: za-(pause)-sshi.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: ざっし
questions.explanation: Well done! ざっし — a short pause at っ.

notes: In a sound lesson with typed reading checks: describe timing in beats, as the long-vowel lesson does, and give how a word sounds in kana (say が, stay silent for one beat on っ, then say こう), not in rōmaji. Rōmaji stays in the kana cards, with one exception: when a sound has no rōmaji of its own, such as the small っ, give one worked example that says how it is typed (In rōmaji, a small っ doubles the next letter, so you type がっこう as gakkou) and leave the other words for the learner to work out. The explanation of a typed reading check may be shown after a wrong answer, so do not open it with praise: give the rōmaji answer (In rōmaji, きっぷ is kippu: the っ doubles the p). Do not write a word's rōmaji in any other explanation or hint, because a typed check asks the learner to read that word. Do not ask "Have you noticed" about a sound the learner has not met yet.

blocks.text:
やま
かわ
とり
わに
ほん

blocks.title: Read this

blocks.text: Nice work getting here! This little word list uses the kana you just learned: の, ま, や, り, わ and ん. Read each word slowly, one kana at a time.
やま is ya-ma, a mountain. かわ is ka-wa, a river. とり is to-ri, a bird. These are real everyday words, so reading them out loud is great practice.
わに is wa-ni, a crocodile. ほん is ho-n, a book. のり is no-ri, that dried seaweed you wrap around rice. Notice how ん at the end of ほん just adds the 'n' sound.
ん almost always sits at the END of a word or syllable, never at the start. If you see ん, you're probably finishing a sound.

templates.hint: In やま, the first kana や says 'ya'.
In やま, the second kana ま says 'ma'.
In とり, the last kana り says 'ri'.
In わに, the first kana わ says 'wa'.
In のり, the first kana の says 'no'.
In ほん, the last kana ん says 'n'.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: やま
questions.explanation: や is 'ya' and ま is 'ma', so やま reads 'yama'.

questions.prompt: In the word list, which word starts with the 'ya' sound?
questions.explanation: やま begins with や, which says 'ya'.

questions.prompt: What is the second kana in やま?
questions.explanation: やま is ya-ma, so the second kana is ま.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: やま
questions.explanation: ま says 'ma', giving 'yama'.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: とり
questions.explanation: と is 'to' and り is 'ri', so とり reads 'tori'.

questions.prompt: Which word ends with the 'ri' sound?
questions.explanation: とり ends with り, which says 'ri'.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: わに
questions.explanation: わ is 'wa' and に is 'ni', so わに reads 'wani'.

questions.prompt: Which kana makes the 'wa' sound?
questions.explanation: わ says 'wa', as in わに.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: のり
questions.explanation: の is 'no' and り is 'ri', so のり reads 'nori'.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the 'no' sound?
questions.explanation: のり begins with の, which says 'no'.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: ほん
questions.explanation: ほ is 'ho' and ん adds the 'n' sound, so ほん reads 'hon'.

questions.prompt: Which kana makes the 'n' sound at the end of ほん?
questions.explanation: ん says 'n' and finishes the word ほん.

notes: Do not write the rōmaji of the passage words in the Teach beat, apart from one worked example (やま is ya-ma): the typed checks ask the learner to read those words with no hint, so every other word gets only its meaning, for example かわ (river). Example blocks always show a reading, so use one only for that worked word and list the others with their meanings in a text block. Every word in the passage gets an English meaning somewhere in the Teach beat. When the targets are kana, they were taught in earlier lessons: do not re-teach them with kana cards or say "meet five new katakana". Build the passage from real everyday words made of those kana, and have the checks read those words. A multiple-choice check never says "type", and no two checks ask for the same word.

blocks.text: Some Japanese words hold a vowel longer. A held vowel takes two beats instead of one, and that extra beat really matters. Try clapping twice while you say it: one clap for each beat. Hold the vowel across both claps so the sound stretches out.
Holding a vowel can completely change a word. A short one-beat vowel and a long two-beat vowel are two different words, so take your time and give the long ones their full length.
Let's meet five family-and-fun words. Start with おかあさん, mother. Clap: お — かあ (hold the あ for two beats) — さん. That doubled あ is the long vowel.
Next, おとうさん, father. Here the long sound is written おう, but おう usually sounds like a long お. So say お — とう (hold a long お across two beats) — さん.
Now おにいさん, older brother. Clap: お — にい (hold the い for two beats) — さん. The doubled い stretches the sound.
Then おねえさん, older sister. Clap: お — ねえ (hold the え for two beats) — さん. Notice おかあさん, おにいさん and おねえさん each repeat the vowel, while おとうさん uses おう.
Last one: えいが, movie. えい usually sounds like a long え, so say a stretched え for two beats, then が: ええ — が. Even though it is written えい, your ear hears a long え.
Two helpers for reading long vowels: えい usually sounds like a long え (as in えいが), and おう usually sounds like a long お (as in おとうさん). The others simply double the vowel you see.

templates.hint: Clap twice: お — かあ — さん. The held あ means 'mother'.
おう sounds like a long お. This one means 'father'.
Hold the い for two beats: お — にい — さん, 'older brother'.
Hold the え for two beats: お — ねえ — さん, 'older sister'.
えい sounds like a long え. This word means 'movie'.

questions.explanation: おかあさん is 'mother'. Hold the あ for two beats: お — かあ — さん.

questions.prompt: Type the word you see: おかあさん
questions.explanation: Clap twice on the held vowel: お — かあ — さん. It means 'mother'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'father'?
questions.explanation: おとうさん is 'father'. おう sounds like a long お: お — とう — さん.

questions.prompt: Type the word you see: おとうさん
questions.explanation: おう usually sounds like a long お. Say お — とう — さん, 'father'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'older brother'?
questions.explanation: おにいさん is 'older brother'. Hold the い for two beats: お — にい — さん.

questions.prompt: Type the word you see: おにいさん
questions.explanation: The doubled い is a long vowel: お — にい — さん, 'older brother'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'older sister'?
questions.explanation: おねえさん is 'older sister'. Hold the え for two beats: お — ねえ — さん.

questions.prompt: Type the word you see: おねえさん
questions.explanation: The doubled え is a long vowel: お — ねえ — さん, 'older sister'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'movie'?
questions.explanation: えいが is 'movie'. えい sounds like a long え: ええ — が.

questions.prompt: Type the word you see: えいが
questions.explanation: えい usually sounds like a long え. Stretch the え for two beats, then が: 'movie'.

notes: Gloss each word the way a learner says it in English: pencil, water, phone, shirt, restaurant. Do not copy dictionary qualifiers such as (wooden), (cool or cold), (undergarment) or (Western-style) into translations or choices. Typed answers are graded kana by kana: おとうさん is otousan and えいが is eiga (otoosan and eega are marked wrong), and a katakana ー doubles the vowel before it (コーヒー is koohii, not kouhii). So never describe a held sound as another spelling (do not write "コー sounds like こう"), and when a typed check asks for a word with a long vowel, say once in the Teach beat that every kana is typed, even one heard as a held sound. A typed prompt never says "in kana" (learners type rōmaji): say "rōmaji is fine", and make the expected answer the only natural one ("ask for tea using ください" when おねがいします would also fit). Never put words from your instructions, such as "from the corpus", into lesson text.

original_draft.title: Is not: じゃありません

blocks.text: You already know how to say what something IS with です. Now let's say what something is NOT. Just swap です for じゃありません. That's it!

blocks.japanese: わたし は いしゃ です。
blocks.reading: わたし は いしゃ です。

blocks.japanese: わたし は いしゃ じゃありません。
blocks.reading: わたし は いしゃ じゃありません。

blocks.text: See how the sentence stays the same, but じゃありません replaces です at the end? じゃありません means "is not" or "am not" or "are not".

blocks.japanese: これ は みず じゃありません。
blocks.reading: これ は みず じゃありません。

blocks.text: Think of the じゃ in じゃありません like a little "no way, nope" sound. じゃ... nope, it's not that.

blocks.label: Listen: です and じゃありません

blocks.japanese: あなた は がくせい じゃありません か。
blocks.reading: あなた は がくせい じゃありません か。

templates.hint: じゃありません turns a です sentence into "is not".

questions.prompt: Which word means "is not"?
questions.explanation: じゃありません means "is not / am not / are not". です means "is".

questions.prompt: What does わたし は いしゃ じゃありません。 mean?
questions.explanation: わたし は いしゃ with じゃありません at the end means "I am not a doctor".

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so it means "This is not a key": これ は かぎ ___。
questions.explanation: To say "is not", you end with じゃありません instead of です.

questions.prompt: Type the Japanese for "I am not a student." (rōmaji is fine). Use わたし は がくせい...
questions.correctAnswer: わたし は がくせい じゃありません。
questions.explanation: わたし は がくせい じゃありません。 swaps です for じゃありません to say "am not".
questions.rubric: Accept if the sentence ends with じゃありません and keeps the order わたし は がくせい. The 。 should come straight after じゃありません.

notes: Do not mark a check open (grading: "open") unless the lesson's author note asks for one: lessons with AI-graded checks can't be published yet. A translation check is closed: name the words to use in the prompt so there is one natural answer (Type the Japanese for "I am not a student." Use わたし and がくせい. Rōmaji is fine.), and store that answer in kana. Spaces and 。 are ignored when it is compared.

blocks.text: Time for family kanji! You already say these words in kana. Now you meet the characters: 子 child, 女 woman, 男 male, 父 father, 母 mother. Let's look at each one.
子 means child. Picture a little kid with arms out and a big round head — that top stroke is the head, the lines below are the body.
女 means woman. See a figure sitting with legs crossed and arms folded — graceful and balanced.
男 means male. The top is 田 (a rice field) and the bottom is 力 (power). A man was the power working in the field.
父 (ちち) means father. Those two crossing strokes at the top look like someone's arms held up, strong and in charge.
母 (はは) means mother. Notice the two dots inside — think of them as the mother holding her child close.

blocks.japanese: ちち は いしゃ です
blocks.reading: ちち は いしゃ です

blocks.japanese: はは は せんせい です
blocks.reading: はは は せんせい です

blocks.label: Listen: 子 女 男 父 母

templates.hint: A little kid with a round head — which kanji?
A figure sitting gracefully — woman.
Field on top, power below — male.
Crossed arms at the top — ちち.
Two dots inside, like holding a child — はは.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means 'child'?
questions.explanation: 子 means child — the round head on top with the body below.

questions.prompt: What does 子 mean?
questions.explanation: 子 means child, as in こども.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means 'woman'?
questions.explanation: 女 means woman — a figure sitting with crossed legs and folded arms.

questions.prompt: What does 女 mean?
questions.explanation: 女 means woman.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means 'male'?
questions.explanation: 男 means male — a rice field on top with power below.

questions.prompt: What is at the bottom of 男, giving it the idea of strength?
questions.explanation: 男 combines field (田) over power (力) — the man working with strength in the field.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means 'father'?
questions.explanation: 父 means father (ちち) — the crossing strokes look like raised arms.

questions.prompt: 父 is read as ちち. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 父 means father and is read ちち when talking about your own dad.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means 'mother'?
questions.explanation: 母 means mother (はは) — notice the two dots inside, like holding a child.

questions.prompt: 母 is read as はは. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 母 means mother and is read はは when talking about your own mom.

notes: Name a part of a kanji as a kanji only when that kanji is listed as taught (子 inside 学, 人 inside 何). Describe any other part in words, by its shape or a taught kana it looks like: the top of 男 is a rice field, a box split into four, and the bottom looks like the katakana カ and means strength. An untaught kanji anywhere, even as a part, is rejected. Give every target kanji at least one reading in kana in the Teach beat (女 is read おんな), and ask for it in a check, because reviews ask the learner to type a reading. Describe strokes as they really are: 小 is a long line down the middle with a short stroke on each side. Only say the learner already knows a word if an earlier lesson taught it. A typed prompt says "Rōmaji is fine", never "in kana".

blocks.text: Let's talk about age and birthdays! You already know the numbers, so saying how old someone is will feel easy. Two new words today: さい (years old) and たんじょうび (birthday).
To give an age, put a number in front of さい. いちさい means 'one year old', じゅうさい means 'ten years old'. Add です to make it a full sentence.

blocks.japanese: わたし は にじゅうごさい です。
blocks.reading: わたし は にじゅうごさい です

blocks.text: The second word is たんじょうび, which means 'birthday'. Notice the small ょ and the long こう-like じょう sound: say たん, then じょう held for two beats, then び.

blocks.japanese: たんじょうび は いつ ですか。
blocks.reading: たんじょうび は いつ ですか

blocks.text: さい sounds like 'sigh' — think of blowing out candles with a happy sigh on your birthday, counting the years.

blocks.label: Listen: さい and たんじょうび

templates.hint: A number goes in front of this word to give an age.
The day you were born.

questions.prompt: What does さい mean?
questions.explanation: さい follows a number to say how old someone is.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'birthday'?
questions.explanation: たんじょうび is 'birthday'. さい means 'years old'.

questions.prompt: Type the Japanese for 'years old'.
questions.explanation: In rōmaji, さい is sai. It goes right after a number.

questions.prompt: Type the Japanese for 'birthday'.
questions.explanation: In rōmaji, たんじょうび is tanjoubi. The じょう holds the long vowel for two beats.

notes: Check sound changes before putting a number in front of a counter: 1, 8 and 10 years old are いっさい, はっさい and じゅっさい, 20 is はたち, and 10,000 is いちまん, never まん on its own. Where a number has a common second word, say so once (よん for four, なな for seven). Never tell the learner they already know or have met this lesson's own words: only words from earlier lessons are known. A mnemonic must be true of the word: don't say one word hides inside another (どう in どうぞ) unless it is built from it. Describe a held sound by the kana that holds it (the い makes け last two beats), never as another spelling (とけい sounds like と・け・え).

blocks.text:
つくえ が あります。
ほん が あります。
かばん が あります。
いす も あります。
blocks.title: Read this

blocks.text: This is a short list of things in a room. Let's read what is there.
Here are the words in the list and what they mean: つくえ (desk), ほん (book), かばん (bag), いす (chair). You already know these — read them out loud slowly.

blocks.japanese: ほん が あります
blocks.reading: ほん が あります (hon ga arimasu)

blocks.text: ～が あります means 'there is' or 'there are' for things (not people). So つくえ が あります means 'there is a desk'. も means 'also', so いす も あります means 'there is a chair, too'.

templates.hint: ～が あります means 'there is' for a thing.
ほん means 'book'.
つくえ means 'desk'.
かばん means 'bag'.

questions.prompt: What does つくえ が あります mean?
questions.explanation: ～が あります means 'there is' for a thing, so つくえ が あります is 'there is a desk'.

questions.prompt: In いす も あります, what does も add?
questions.explanation: も means 'also', so いす も あります means 'there is a chair, too'.

notes: The Teach beat must not answer the checks. Don't translate a passage line that a check asks about, and don't say what the passage is about if a check asks it. Explain the grammar with a sentence that is not in the passage (みず が あります is 'there is water'), give each passage word its meaning, and leave the passage itself for the learner to read.

original_draft.title: Is not: じゃありません

blocks.text: You already know how to say what something IS with です. Now let's say what something is NOT. Just swap です for じゃありません. That's it!

blocks.japanese: わたし は いしゃ です。
blocks.reading: わたし は いしゃ です。

blocks.japanese: わたし は いしゃ じゃありません。
blocks.reading: わたし は いしゃ じゃありません。

blocks.text: See how the sentence stays the same, but じゃありません replaces です at the end? じゃありません means "is not" or "am not" or "are not".

blocks.japanese: これ は みず じゃありません。
blocks.reading: これ は みず じゃありません。

blocks.text: Think of the じゃ in じゃありません like a little "no way, nope" sound. じゃ... nope, it's not that.

blocks.label: Listen: です and じゃありません

blocks.japanese: あなた は がくせい じゃありません か。
blocks.reading: あなた は がくせい じゃありません か。

templates.hint: じゃありません turns a です sentence into "is not".

questions.prompt: Which word means "is not"?
questions.explanation: じゃありません means "is not / am not / are not". です means "is".

questions.prompt: What does わたし は いしゃ じゃありません。 mean?
questions.explanation: わたし は いしゃ with じゃありません at the end means "I am not a doctor".

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so it means "This is not a key": これ は かぎ ___。
questions.explanation: To say "is not", you end with じゃありません instead of です.

questions.prompt: Type the Japanese for "I am not a student." (rōmaji is fine). Use わたし は がくせい...
questions.correctAnswer: わたし は がくせい じゃありません。
questions.explanation: わたし は がくせい じゃありません。 swaps です for じゃありません to say "am not".
questions.rubric: Accept if the sentence ends with じゃありません and keeps the order わたし は がくせい. The 。 should come straight after じゃありません.

notes: Every Japanese word in examples, choices and checks must already be taught: これ comes after the じゃありません lesson, and くるま is never taught. A meaning check whose answer depends on an untaught word can only be guessed. Teach one point: don't add a second one such as a negative question (〜じゃありません か), whose はい and いいえ answers confuse beginners. A mnemonic must be true: じゃ doesn't mean "nope". In a translation check, name the words to use and store the one natural answer in kana.
